content.text:
You are a Capcom NES animator (Mega Man 2-3). The image shows the 2 frames of a looping enemy
animation, left to right (enlarged; the grey-blue background is not part of the sprite). Frame 1 is the approved
still.

The enemy: A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes.
The motion: swim in pulses: frame 1 (the approved still) is the glide, tentacles together; frame 2 is the stroke, tentacles flared out wide as it pushes; looping
Its behaviour in the game: moves toward Mega Man in pulses about every 40 game frames: a short gather (tentacles flare, a brief tell), then a quick stroke that shoots it forward and a long glide that slows down with the tentacles together

Decide how long each frame is held, in game frames at 60 fps (whole numbers). Capcom NES enemies hold frames for
roughly 4-16 game frames in steady cycles, and hold poses longer where the behaviour pauses or glides. Make the
rhythm express the behaviour.

Return ONLY a JSON object: {"durations": [frame 1, frame 2, ...], "rationale": "one or two sentences"}

message.content: {"durations": [28, 12], "rationale": "The pulse cycle is about 40 game frames. Frame 1 (glide, tentacles together) is held for 28 frames as the long, slowing coast. Frame 2 (flared stroke) is held for 12 frames as the short gather-and-thrust burst, so the loop totals 40 and matches the behaviour.", "note": "Total loop = 40 frames."}
